nodes.name: Smartypants
nodes.what: Shows the system an agent is designing, and where the code that landed left that request
nodes.why: Engineers need a picture of what the agent is building while it is still coding

nodes.name: Hook pipeline
nodes.what: Watches each prompt and edit, and updates the diagram without stopping the turn
nodes.why: The picture has to move with the agent, and the agent has to keep working if the picture fails

nodes.name: Design model
nodes.what: Stores the system, its components, and their modules, each with a what and a why
nodes.why: The hooks and the canvas need one shared picture, not a new guess on every turn

nodes.name: Flavor adapters
nodes.what: Sends the floor and the ladder to exactly one of Claude, Codex, Grok, Muse, or Pi
nodes.why: The config picks the builder, and a bad flavor must not silently call another

nodes.name: Memory ledger
nodes.what: Remembers the baseline and later deltas as short gists
nodes.why: A hook added mid-project needs to track what changed without keeping transcripts

nodes.name: Canvas
nodes.what: Draws the design on a desktop surface you can pan and zoom
nodes.why: The diagram is how an engineer sees what the agent is building

nodes.name: Host normalizer
nodes.what: Turns Claude, Codex, Grok, Muse, and Pi events into one user message or one delivered edit
nodes.why: Five hosts should feed one pipeline instead of five different diagrams

nodes.name: Config gate
nodes.what: Reads smartypants.config.json and stays quiet when that file is missing or invalid
nodes.why: The hook should do nothing until someone turns it on in that project

nodes.name: Re-entry guard
nodes.what: Returns immediately while a builder turn is already running
nodes.why: Muse and Pi would otherwise start another builder from the hook they just fired

nodes.name: Depth floor
nodes.what: Keeps the diagram at system, or system and components, or system through module
nodes.why: The picture should stop at the level the config asked for, and module is the usual stop

nodes.name: Drift flags
nodes.what: Records the intent and how the delivered code differs, once for each divergence
nodes.why: An engineer needs to see where the build left the request, including code that fits no node

nodes.name: Request builder
nodes.what: Puts the floor, the ladder, and the ledger gists into that one flavor's request
nodes.why: The builder has to use this project's depth, not invent files and functions as nodes

nodes.name: Gist
nodes.what: Keeps the useful words from a turn and drops the filler
nodes.why: The memory has to stay about the project, not the chatter around it

nodes.name: Compaction
nodes.what: Folds older gists once the ledger passes about ten thousand tokens
nodes.why: The history sent on the next turn has to stay small

nodes.name: Seed sketch
nodes.what: Names the files already in the tree so the first diagram matches the project
nodes.why: A baseline has to come from the code that is there before later turns track deltas

nodes.name: Scene layout
nodes.what: Places each module inside its component and each component inside the system
nodes.why: The picture has to show containment, not a flat list of names

nodes.name: Pan and zoom
nodes.what: Lets you drag and scroll across the desktop surface
nodes.why: A system diagram grows past one screen
